references.text: Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is a common ritual act that symbolizes identification with the sacrifice and the transfer of sin.
The same ritual of laying hands on the animal's head before slaughter for the peace offering.
Parallel text regarding laying on of hands for the sin offering of the anointed priest.
A similar ritual for a sin offering from an ordinary person, with laying on of hands on the sacrificial animal's head.
The same procedure involving laying on of hands and slaughter at the place of burnt offerings for the sin offering.
The place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the Lord, north of the altar, as referred to in the verse.
Laying on of hands on the scapegoat on the Day of Atonement, where sins are transferred to the animal.
Laying on of hands on the sin offering goat during the consecration of priests.
The New Testament explains that under the law almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
Reference to the sin offering animals whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest.
